title: Maui Research and Technology Park land designation
summary: On October 21, 2026, Bill 141 (2026) was the main item. It would move part of the Maui Research and Technology Park's commercial land into the Residential District, growing it from 102.3 to 158 acres, with the 1,250-home cap unchanged. The Maui Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval on September 8, after the council sent the zoning change to it in May.

timeline.text: The chair said the residential area would grow from 102.3 acres to 158 acres.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The cap of 1,250 residential units stays the same.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The bill would also allow minor medical centers in the park's civic district.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The top reason given for the bill was to switch part of the park's commercial land to residential land.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The main item was Bill 141 (2026), which would amend the county code chapter for the Maui Research and Technology Park.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The September 8th meeting will include a council resolution and zoning changes for the Maui Research and Technology Park.
The director said the department could talk with the research park's landowner if the commission takes up the map again later.
A second motion to designate the whole park special purpose district also failed.
The planning director said special purpose district is absolutely inappropriate for the park.
